### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **1** package(s): `@objectstack/service-analytics`, touching **2** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/services/service-analytics/src/dataset-date-bucket-door.ts`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

⛔ **2** release-owned page(s) name something this change touched. These are **read-only**:

- `content/docs/releases/v14.mdx`  _(via generateSql (symbol, a method of class FallbackDelegateStrategy))_
- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-5.mdx`  _(via generateSql (symbol, a method of class FallbackDelegateStrategy))_

> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/services/service-analytics/src/dataset-date-bucket-door.ts`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **1** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **60** of **216** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **156** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **156**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **101** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **10** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 94d3e2543488fceda39fbfe88036bb6887037390` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `67527b6e77da522487e106657719201704802267` — the merge of head `1074fbba63d89cc178a9f8fbc3f579333f89c16b` into base `94d3e2543488fceda39fbfe88036bb6887037390`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 67527b6e77da522487e106657719201704802267 && git checkout 67527b6e77da522487e106657719201704802267
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 94d3e2543488fceda39fbfe88036bb6887037390 1074fbba63d89cc178a9f8fbc3f579333f89c16b && git checkout -B drift-repro 94d3e2543488fceda39fbfe88036bb6887037390 && git merge --no-ff 1074fbba63d89cc178a9f8fbc3f579333f89c16b

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 94d3e2543488fceda39fbfe88036bb6887037390
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 94d3e2543488fceda39fbfe88036bb6887037390` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `1074fbba63d89cc178a9f8fbc3f579333f89c16b`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/services/service-analytics/src/analytics-service.ts, packages/services/service-analytics/src/dataset-date-bucket-door.ts, packages/services/service-analytics/src/__tests__/fallback-delegate-date-bucket-type.test.ts, .changeset/29364-fallback-date-bucket-refused-alike.md + packages/objectql/src/aggregate-query-shape-door.ts, packages/objectql/src/having-filter.ts (`classOfDeclaredType`), packages/objectql/src/engine.ts (the aggregate door order), packages/drivers/driver-memory/src/memory-analytics.ts (the time-bucket fold), packages/drivers/driver-memory/src/in-memory-strategy.ts, packages/services/service-analytics/src/strategies/objectql-strategy.ts (`aggregateGroupKeys`, `aggregateObjectOf`, the dry-run door call), packages/services/service-analytics/src/strategies/types.ts, packages/services/service-analytics/src/plugin.ts (`sourceFieldMeta`, capabilities, fallback capture), packages/spec/src/contracts/analytics-service.ts (`StrategyContext.fallbackService`), packages/spec/src/data/search-fields.ts, packages/spec/src/data/field-value.zod.ts

Inputs read: card #29364 (body, triage 6580338408, claims 6581347422 / 6581400785, Step 0 report 6581581002, seat ruling 6581612223 letter A, dev report 6582608728); PR #29500 body, file list, net diff `origin/main...1074fbba` (4 files, +281/-0; merge base `aca58cdb`); the check-runs on the head; the cited code read on `origin/main` `73c24394`. Not the dispatch order, not the dispatching seat's conclusions. PR author `objectstack-fleet[bot]`.

### ① Derived judgments

Each change the diff implies to an accept set or a public surface, judged against the cited code:

1. **Fallback `execute` refuses a date bucket over a formula or a non-date/datetime field before delegating — right.** `assertDelegatedDateBucketsTemporal` runs first in `FallbackDelegateStrategy.execute` and throws the service door's refusal (`dataset-date-bucket-door.ts`), so `ctx.fallbackService.query` is never reached (`analytics-service.ts` L5031-5061). Pinned on both public construction paths with `delegate.query` never called.
2. **Fallback `generateSql` refuses alike — right.** The door runs before the `fallbackService.generateSql` branch and before the "SQL generation not supported" stub, so a host whose delegate renders no SQL is refused the same way (L5063-5070). Pinned with `delegate.generateSql` never called.
3. **Field for field with the engine face — holds, for every declared type.** The service door (`dataset-date-bucket-door.ts`) judges virtual first (`isVirtualSearchField({ type })`, `SEARCH_VIRTUAL_TYPES = {formula}`, type-only in spec `search-fields.ts` L159), then `type === undefined || CALENDAR_DATE_TYPES || INSTANT_TYPES → pass`, else refuse. The engine door (`aggregate-query-shape-door.ts` L145-174) judges virtual first with the same spec predicate on the field def, then `classOfDeclaredType` (`having-filter.ts` L1150): `formula → undefined` (already caught), `date → 'date'`, `datetime → 'datetime'`, `time/numeric/boolean → their class`, **everything else → `'text'`**, so file, image, json, lookup, multi-option and select fields are refused on both doors with the same "is a declared TYPE field — only a date or datetime field can be date-bucketed" sentence. The two message templates, code (`INVALID_FIELD`), `status`/`httpStatus` 400, `object`, `param: 'groupBy'`, `path: groupBy.N.dateGranularity`, `field`, `fields` are identical (compared as strings side by side; the new test `toEqual`s the engine's actual refusal on the same real ObjectQL + SQLite engine). Positions are the engine's because the keys are `aggregateGroupKeys(query, cube)`, the ObjectQL strategy's direct-path builder; the `groupBy.1` case is pinned.
4. **Nothing that should still be answered is now refused — right.**
   - a real `date` or `datetime` bucket: `CALENDAR_DATE_TYPES`/`INSTANT_TYPES` pass; the datetime control is pinned on both faces (rows and dry-run statement pass through unchanged).
   - a lookup-traversed dimension (`account.created_at`): `resolveCubeFieldName` yields the dotted spelling, `sourceFieldMeta(object, 'account.created_at')` reads `fields['account.created_at']` → `undefined` → not judged; the engine's `declaredFieldClasses` has no such key either → not judged. Consistent (and `assertDimensionJoinsBacked` in `callCtx` still governs the path, on every strategy).
   - a host with no field types: `declaredFieldType` is `config.sourceFieldMeta?.(…)?.type` (L1647) → `undefined` → `continue`; pinned ("no-types host not judged"), the same stand-down the preview and dry run take and the engine takes for a registry-less host.
   - a cube whose `sql` is not a bare object name, or a dimension whose `sql` is an expression: `getObject` finds nothing → `undefined` → not judged. Same as the preview.
   - `query.cube` is always set here: `ensureCube` (L3699) registers or 404s before any strategy, so `ctx.getCube(query.cube!)` resolves and the `if (!cube) return` guard is a harmless belt.
5. **No third copy of the predicate — right.** `git grep` for `CALENDAR_DATE_TYPES|isVirtualSearchField|only a date or datetime field can be date-bucketed` across service-analytics, driver-memory and objectql finds the engine door, the one service door (`dataset-date-bucket-door.ts`) and their tests only. The new helper is module-local (`function`, not exported), makes one call to `assertDatasetDateBucketsTemporal`, and introduces no message text.
6. **Order on the fallback face vs the engine face — consistent for this door.** The engine runs `assertDateBucketTargetsAreTemporal` before `assertAggregatedColumnsAreDistinct` (`engine.ts` L21350-21351); the fallback face runs only the date door, so a query carrying both faults is refused on the date ground on both faces. (The dry run and preview run the column door first; that pre-existing divergence between the engine and the service's other two faces is not this PR's.)
7. **Public surface — unchanged, as declared.** No export, type, config key, error code or status is added or removed; `dataset-date-bucket-door.ts` changes only a doc comment; `StrategyContext` (spec) and `DatasetScopedStrategyContext` are untouched (the commit `1074fbba` reads `declaredFieldType` through the dataset-scoped cast as `ObjectQLStrategy.generateSql` does, L805). `check:api-surface` has nothing to see; `Check Changeset` and the PR-body guards are green.
8. **The twin `InMemoryStrategy` (`@objectstack/driver-memory`) stays door-less — not reached while `fallbackService` is set.** It delegates to `ctx.fallbackService.query` at priority 30 (`in-memory-strategy.ts` L17-37). The chain is `[...builtIn, ...custom].sort(by priority)` (L1716-1725): the built-in `FallbackDelegateStrategy` is pushed whenever `fallbackService` is configured and precedes any custom strategy at the same priority under the stable sort, so `resolveStrategy` lands on the doored strategy first; `InMemoryStrategy` without a `fallbackService` throws rather than delegating. Correct today, but it rests on sort stability and array order and the `AnalyticsServiceConfig.fallbackService` doc still says "Used by InMemoryStrategy" (L906-908). See ④ should-fix 1.

### ② Semver level

- Changeset `.changeset/29364-fallback-date-bucket-refused-alike.md`: `'@objectstack/service-analytics': patch`; title with `!`; line-initial `Clause-②: no (narrowing)` with the refusal, the measured before, the reach and "nothing is widened"; line-initial `Metadata-protocol: none`; `**BREAKING**` banner; exactly one ADR-0087 marker, an HTML comment reading `adr-0087: not-required (no-migration-prescription)` with its reason. The PR body carries the same two declaration lines, line-initial.
- Level matches the rule: a non-protocol change (`Metadata-protocol: none`) ships `patch` and keeps its BREAKING banner and ADR-0087 disposition. Correct — nothing an author can write changes; the cube and query schemas are untouched.
- The disposition is honest: no spec key, export, type or stored row is added, removed, renamed or re-shaped, so `objectstack migrate meta` has nothing to rewrite and no tombstone is owed. The "remedy" paragraph is a query-level fix (bucket a date field), not a consumer-code rewrite, so it does not contradict `no-migration-prescription`; `Check Changeset` (which runs `check-adr-0087-registration.mjs --base`) is green on the head.
- The declared reach is right: the default `AnalyticsServicePlugin` composition advertises `objectqlAggregate: !!executeAggregate` and always bridges `executeAggregate` (`plugin.ts` L322-360, L531-535), so `ObjectQLStrategy` (priority 20) takes every bucketed query to the engine; the fallback face is reached only via `new AnalyticsService({ fallbackService })` or a `queryCapabilities` override with `objectqlAggregate: false` beside a pre-registered analytics service (L311-316). No in-repo non-test code does either.
- `Skills-docs: none` holds: no `skills/**` or `content/docs/**` page describes the fallback face as able to date-bucket a formula or text field. The docs-drift bot lists two release-owned pages that merely name `FallbackDelegateStrategy.generateSql`; release notes are release-owned and not for this PR.

### ③ Boundary flags

- **Dev flag: dogfood red on 2 files (`flow-runas.dogfood.test.ts` 3 cases, `declarative-endpoint-anonymous-guest.dogfood.test.ts` 1 case), red on the base leg too, re-pointed on `main` by #29451.** Verified against the tree, not the report: `6af3d2957` ("re-point the runAs and anonymous-guest flow pins to flow start admission's record rule", #29451) is in `aca58cdb..origin/main` and touches exactly those two test files plus `fixtures/flow-runas-fixture.ts` (207/27, test-only, skip-changeset). Neither reads analytics; this diff touches nothing outside `packages/services/service-analytics` and a changeset. The reading holds. **No main merge is required before landing:** the merge group builds the merge of this head into `main`, which already carries the re-point, and the PR's "Dogfood Regression Gate" check is green on the head (its shards are skipped on PRs by design; per #29451's own body they do not run in the queue either). A rebase would change nothing in the 4 files (`git diff --stat aca58cdb origin/main -- packages/services/service-analytics packages/drivers/driver-memory packages/objectql` is empty for the first two and touches no door in the third).
- **Dev `open_questions`: none on the done report.** The Step 0 question (fix / close / retire) was ruled A on record 6581612223; the diff implements A as ordered: one call to the existing door, in `execute` and `generateSql`, no third copy, no spec edit, `Clause-②: no (narrowing)`, BREAKING banner, one ADR-0087 marker, pins through both public construction paths.
- **Dev out-of-scope observation: the column-asked-twice door (`assertDatasetGroupColumnsDistinct`) is not in front of the delegate.** Correct as declared and correctly not added here (the ruling's build order names the date door alone). Escalated as a should-fix follow-up in ④, not a FAIL.
- **Dev deviation: the second ablation leg ran at `cf460c16`, not `1074fbba`.** `git log origin/main..1074fbba` shows the two commits; `1074fbba` changes only the `declaredFieldType` read (through the `DatasetScopedStrategyContext` cast) — the same runtime behaviour, since the service's `baseCtx` always carries it as an arrow. Not re-run (read-only); the claim is consistent with the diff.
- **Dev deviation: no assignee/reviewer set** — the standard order forbids it; fine.
- **Check-runs on the head** (conclusions are the gate verdicts): every completed run is `success` or `skipped` — Check Changeset, Check PR Size, PR-body guards, Governed Surface Queue Guard, Auto Label, Flag docs, Lint · scoped (tooling self-tests, PM dispatch-gates, query-options erasure, slot lookup & corpus), Lint · ESLint, Lint · docs & code guards, Lint · repo & tooling gates, Lint · CI/release/engine gates, Type Check · debt ledger / consumer gates / source gates, Build Core, Plan Test Core shards, Test UI / Dogfood Regression Gate / Live E2E UI (aggregators green, shards skipped). Polled until completion: all 48 check-runs on the head are completed — 35 `success`, 13 `skipped` (UI, docs, Temporal Conformance, 18.x harness, schedule gate, matrix placeholders), 0 failed, 0 still in progress; Test Core (1-8/8), Build Core and Type Check · workspace landed green during this review.
- **Author** is `objectstack-fleet[bot]` (the relay), so no off-relay login is named.

### ④ Design judgment

The narrowing read against the published spec on `main` and the live tree, not the PR's account:

- **It makes the spec's own refusal real; it takes no declared capability away.** The spec's `StrategyContext.fallbackService` (`packages/spec/src/contracts/analytics-service.ts` L521-528) declares only `query`, `getMeta`, optional `generateSql` — a delegate, not a promise that a time dimension may bucket a non-date column. The cube contract's `time` dimension and `DateGranularity` name a bucket over a date; the engine door's header states the rule ("only a date or datetime field can be date-bucketed") and `#29167` extended it to virtual fields on every face that reaches the engine or the service door. Before this head the fallback face was the one face where a `time` dimension over a `formula` returned 200 with every row in one `null` group — the exact "plausible table under 200" the engine door exists to refuse. Narrowing it to the same refusal is the spec's reading, with the engine's own words and remedy, on both the query and the dry run.
- **Tried to break it:**
  - *Reader parity.* The fallback face reads types through `ctx.declaredFieldType`, which is `sourceFieldMeta(...).type` — the same hook the preview and dry-run doors read and the plugin fills from `getObject(...).fields[field].type` (`plugin.ts` L1437-1440), i.e. the same declaration the engine door reads. No second reading.
  - *Key parity.* `aggregateGroupKeys` is the direct path's builder (dimensions in order, then bucketed time dimensions not already listed, deduplicated by `pushGroupKey`), so a bucket at `groupBy.1` lands at the engine's position; pinned. The cross-object key builder is not used here, and it need not be: a cross-object dimension becomes an un-bucketed FK column on that path, and a dotted dimension is not judged on either face (①.4).
  - *Over-refusal.* `date`/`datetime` pass; a no-types host passes; an undeclared or dotted field passes; `time` is refused on both faces (`CLOCK_TIME_TYPES` is neither set; the engine classes it `'time'`). No case found where the fallback refuses and the engine serves, or the reverse, for a declared type.
  - *Door before admission?* No: the strategy runs after `callCtx`, so exposure, read admission, internal-field, stored-metadata-body, joins-backed, relationship-column and order-key doors all precede it, as for every other strategy; a field the caller may not read keeps its 403.
  - *The delegate's own vocabulary.* `MemoryAnalyticsService` still refuses sub-day granularities with `unsupportedTimeGranularityError` (`memory-analytics.ts` L1176-1178); that door is untouched and runs after this one, so a formula bucket at `hour` is now refused for the field, not the granularity — the engine's order too.
- **Findings**
  - **should-fix 1 — the door-less twin.** `@objectstack/driver-memory`'s exported `InMemoryStrategy` delegates to `ctx.fallbackService.query` with no door, at the same priority 30; it is shadowed by the built-in `FallbackDelegateStrategy` only through the stable sort's built-in-before-custom order, and `AnalyticsServiceConfig.fallbackService`'s doc still says "Used by InMemoryStrategy". Either retire the twin (it is unreachable for delegation whenever it could delegate) or state the shadowing where the chain is built, so a later re-ordering cannot re-open this face. New card for the server lane; not this PR's scope (the ruling bounded the build to the service's strategy, and driver-memory cannot import the service door).
  - **should-fix 2 — the column-asked-twice door on the fallback face.** `assertDatasetGroupColumnsDistinct` guards the preview, the dry run and (via the engine) the ObjectQL face, but not the delegate: a column raw beside its own bucket, or two buckets of one column, is handed to the delegate's fold. Measure first on the fallback face (as the dev's observation says), then put the existing door in front of the delegate the same way. New card; the dev named it out of scope under the ruling, correctly.
  - No must-fix.
